chapter_title: Concerning the Catechumen who found fault with the

spiritual_reading.full_translation:
So it is with those who are being reformed. They are divine in measure as they remain steadfast in a living reception of what is Divine. The Divine that has been implanted in them flows down from higher degrees and abides within their interiors.

Yet when their lower mind is stirred into unrest, and the will is heated by injured self-regard, they turn against one another and send forth condemnations from falsity. Do not let this disturb your inner peace. You know conclusively that they are held, for a time, in an outward form of life that is not yet wholly made their own, and they feel aversion toward the inherited and acquired tendency to evil that drives the mind to serve what is alien to heaven. From this conflict they are provoked, and the bitterness that lies in the natural self breaks out into harsh speech face to face.

For you have been admitted into the arcanum of the two opposing principles within the human mind, and you understand that both the inclination toward good and the inclination toward evil are present in every person. You also understand that those who are being made holy sustain a heavy spiritual labor within their operative powers, because they endure the weight of this combat while they are still being held in an external life not yet fully conjoined to their inward renewal.

Your powers of action remain at liberty to resist and subdue the assault upon saving truth and Divine love.

For when contention rises among those who are in the good of religion, it is because the former self still lives in their external degree; and from this they take offence and fall into mutual opposition, and so they enter into disputes with one another.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Coherent throughout as a single teaching on regeneration: the implanted Divine within the reformed, the recurring flare-ups from the lower self, the doctrine of two opposing inclinations in each person, an exhortation to active resistance, and a closing explanation that disputes arise from the lingering former self in externals.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential substrate: a functional psychological-spiritual teaching about mixed states in the elect/reformed (divinity implanted from above; conflict arising from the ‘foreign’ body; two essences in each person; burden-bearing). No narrative seam, no jurisdictional cataloguing, no administrative markers.
findings.evidence: Text teaches by interior function and state: “The divinity that is planted in them came to them from the heights and [ab]elt in them” (¶5); the elect are “established in a body that is not their own… dwell in a foreign land” (¶6); “the mystery of the two essences… what is good and what is evil dwell in every person” (¶7). The spiritual reading does not report a break here; it reads straight through as one account of regeneration and mixed impulses, only noting a mild image-pressure around “foreign land,” which is normal Manichaean idiom rather than a voice shift.

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty (compressed symbol) rather than an insertion: the phrase is abrupt but still fits the chapter’s functional logic as a practical pivot from diagnosis (why quarrels happen) to response (what the hearer can do). The ‘shift’ the reading noted is rhetorical, not textual corruption.
findings.evidence: The spiritual reading flags: “SHIFTS… exhorting the listener’s own agency” and notes it had to ‘synthesize’ “Cross of Light.” But the underlying text is still functional rather than administrative: “Your hands are always free to beat the Cross of Light.” This is not governance/jurisdiction language and contains no named powers or stations; it is an embodied-action metaphor (“hands… beat”) consistent with correspondential instruction about practice amid temptation/conflict. The abruptness is explainable as an aphoristic exhortation, not as a pasted administrative block.

findings.diagnosis: Clean continuation and closure: it restates the causal mechanism of quarrels (the ‘old man’ remaining in the body) in the same correspondential mode as ¶6-¶7. No sign of administrative overlay or seam-expansion.
findings.evidence: “For when quarrelling will arise among the saints [it is] because the old man too dwells in their body; and due to this they shall take offence… they {dispute} with one another.” This matches ¶6’s causality (“Due to this they shall be angry… utter hard words”) and ¶7’s two-essence anthropology. The spiritual reading reports no stumble here, only a standard interpretive gloss (“old man” = former self).

textual_criticism.summary: No textual-critical disruptions detected (0 excisions, 0 annotations). All paragraphs read in a single correspondential voice. The only noted ‘stumble’ (¶8, ‘Cross of Light’) is a symbolic compression and rhetorical pivot, not evidence of an administrative insertion or seam-expansion.

harmonized_paragraphs.text: This is also the case with the elect. They are gods as they stand firm in the image of the gods. The divinity that is planted in them came to them from the heights and [ab]elt in them.

Further, when they will be troubled and angry and resentful, [they] curse each other. However, do not you be troubled in your heart. You know, once and for all, they are established in a body that is not their own, hating the Flesh of Sin that makes the other dwell in a foreign land. Due to this they shall be angry, and say and utter hard words to each others' faces.

For you have known the mystery of the two essences, you have understood that what is good and what is evil dwell in every person. You have also understood that the saints bear a great burden on their shoulders. For you yourself have understood that they carry a great burden, they are established in the body that is not their own.
Your hands are always free to beat the Cross of Light.

For when quarrelling will arise among the saints [it is] because the old man too dwells in their body; and due to this they shall take offence [and fall into mutual opposition,] they {dispute} with one another.
